QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_4

question.text: For a non-institutional client in cash-settled IRD on G-Sec in the 8-11 year maturity bucket, the open interest is INR 10,000 crore. What is the maximum permissible client-level position?

explanation.text: The Logic: For relevant non-institutional clients in cash-settled IRD on G-Sec, the workbook prescribes 3% of open interest or INR 400 crore (for the 8-11 year bucket), whichever is higher. 3% of INR 10,000 crore = INR 300 crore. Higher of INR 300 crore and INR 400 crore = INR 400 crore. The Trap: INR 300 crore applies only the percentage. INR 200 crore is the absolute floor for the 4-8 / 11-15 year buckets, not the 8-11 year bucket. INR 500 crore is not a source-backed client cap. The rule is "whichever is higher", not lower, and it is open-interest based - not based on outstanding stock. Note: Pages 234-235 specify client limits as 3% of open interest or INR 400 crore (8-11 year) / INR 200 crore (4-8 and 11-15 year) - higher of. Page 237 reinforces the open-interest based monitoring.
